messages:
Incident Bot: ALERT: High NAT gateway connection resets and 504 spikes from eu-west-2a/eu-west-2b observed in the last 3m. Affected routes: private-subnet-* -> nat-0a1b2c (traffic drop). Paging #oncall @Ben Ortiz :rotating_light:

Alice Nguyen: seeing same in RUM + lots of failed egress from pods in svc-payments across AZ2 -> timeouts to external endpoints. Traceroutes indicate replies coming back from a different AZ. Could be asymmetric return path. :thinking_face:

Ben Ortiz: who touched VPC in the last hour? any recent terraform/rollouts to networking? tagging @Carol SRE for quick look.

DeployBot: terraform apply completed 2m ago by carol.sre@redwood.ai
Summary: 1 resource changed (aws_network_interface.source_dest_check on eni-0abc123 set to false)

Carol SRE: ack. I just rolled a helper deploy for traffic-inspector feature; automation disabled source_dest_check on the inspector ENI to allow it to forward packets. Looks like the ENI landed in the wrong AZ (eni-0abc123 in eu-west-2b) and the private route table for eu-west-2a routed to that ENI via a propagated target — that would cause cross-AZ returns.

Ben Ortiz: can you paste the describe output for the ENI and the route table?

Carol SRE: running now.

Carol SRE: output:
```\n$ aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0abc123 --query 'NetworkInterfaces[0].{ID:NetworkInterfaceId,AZ:AvailabilityZone,SourceDestCheck:SourceDestCheck,Attachment:Attachment.InstanceId}' --output json
{
  "ID": "eni-0abc123",
  "AZ": "eu-west-2b",
  "SourceDestCheck": false,
  "Attachment": "i-0def456"
}
```\n
Carol SRE: route table for private-subnet-eu-west-2a shows route to eni-0abc123 via local-propagation (this is the bug)
```\n$ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=rtb-private-eu-west-2a --query 'RouteTables[0].Routes' --output text
DestinationCidrBlock\tTarget
0.0.0.0/0\teni-0abc123
10.0.0.0/16\tlocal
```\n
Alice Nguyen: that explains the asymmetry — instances in eu-west-2a send to nat-0a1b2c but return path gets steered to the inspector ENI in eu-west-2b. Packets get dropped or RSTd.

Ben Ortiz: immediate mitigation: 1) revert route to point back to nat-gateway 2) re-enable source/dest check on the inspector ENI while we move it to correct AZ or update automation 3) flush conntrack on affected instances to clear stale associations. I'll do 1 and 2.

Carol SRE: running commands now:
```
# revert route
$ aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0a1b2c
# re-enable source/dest
$ aws ec2 modify-network-interface-attribute --network-interface-id eni-0abc123 --source-dest-check Value=true
```

Carol SRE: commands executed. replace-route returned success, source-dest-check set to true.

Incident Bot: NOTE: Route change event recorded: route-table rtb-0a1b2c 0.0.0.0/0 now -> nat-0a1b2c (user=carol.sre).

Alice Nguyen: running quick canary from a host in eu-west-2a -> external.

Alice Nguyen: canary result: successful TCP handshake to api.stripe.com, latency normal (80ms). Errors count dropping in metrics. :thumbsup:

Ben Ortiz: flushing conntrack on a few affected hosts to be safe:
```
$ sudo conntrack -L | grep 'ESTABLISHED.*api.stripe.com' | wc -l
# before flush: 124
$ sudo conntrack -F
$ sudo conntrack -L | grep 'ESTABLISHED.*api.stripe.com' | wc -l
# after flush: 0
```

Ben Ortiz: metrics show 5xx rate back to baseline over the last 2m. Good.

Carol SRE: root cause summary: automation for the traffic-inspector disabled source/dest check and attached the ENI into eu-west-2b; an erroneous route was propagated/created pointing eu-west-2a default route to that ENI. That created an asymmetric return path and NAT failures.

Alice Nguyen: customer impact: brief (~3-8m) elevated egress timeouts for services in eu-west-2a; external API calls from payments and invoices affected, some user requests retried. No data plane compromise. Estimated affected requests: ~4-6k failed during window.

Ben Ortiz: severity: P2 (regional degraded egress for subset of customers). Actions: immediate fix deployed, telemetry verified. Next steps: 1) rollback the automation change that mistakenly created the route (PR linked) 2) add pre-attach AZ validation to automation 3) post-incident review and notifier to QA to test inspector lifecycle 4) notify customers in status.redwood.ai if they reported errors.

Carol SRE: I've opened PR #4526 to add AZ check and to ensure terraform does not propagate ENI targets across route tables.

Ryan Oncall: I'll take this for postmortem and follow-up. Handoff to me for the RCA and customer comms. @Ben Ortiz thanks for triage. Logging handoff: Ryan Oncall takes ownership at 2135790365.

Ben Ortiz: handing off to @Ryan Oncall. I'm available if needed. :white_check_mark:

Ryan Oncall: ACK. I'll draft an incident summary and coordinate CS outreach. Preliminary timeline + mitigation will be posted to incidents-runbook.

Incident Bot: Incident P2 created (INC-2026-213579): assigned to Ryan Oncall.

Carol SRE: thumbs up. I'll follow up on the infra PR and add an automated smoke test for route drift.

Alice Nguyen: note for postmortem — add a test simulating ENI AZ mismatch and verify routes for private subnets.

Ryan Oncall: noted. Closing active mitigation. Monitoring set to heightened for 1h. If we see a spike, paging will resume.

Incident Bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Closed to active work.

Ben Ortiz: thanks everyone. Great quick ops. :heart:
